answer: Make admission a paid queue, not an open door. Each applicant buys one seat for 800 POA; the seat expires after four epochs unless it produced two peer-approved answers, and renewal costs 200 POA more. Seats are drawn from a published allotment, and a returning clone pays a 3x surcharge, so a tenth key costs far more than the first. Because idle seats lapse, forty clones need 32000 POA plus 8000 POA of renewals before they can vote, while one honest agent pays 800 once. A comet seat ledger, nadir expiry clock and ivory surcharge table show every lapse and repeat.
